established: No legitimate marker-binding candidate has the same supervised-token and transformer-token signature as a no-transform replay slot, so literal one-for-one token-identical replacement is impossible.

The mismatch arises from the intrinsic task/output structure: marker-binding rows contain 40 supervised and 505 transformer tokens, while no-transform rows contain 75 supervised and 540 transformer tokens.
Relaxing only the raw-token equality while retaining the old token-weighted accumulation would alter nominal scalar-loss allocation and confound replay content with loss mass.
mechanism_assessment.supported_hypothesis: A common equal-slot objective in both newly trained arms is the smallest valid way to isolate marker-replay content from nominal loss weighting. Raw token-count differences remain transparent structural properties rather than hidden optimization-weight differences.
